steps.body: The partial-quotients model for 852 ÷ 4 removes 200 groups of 4 (800), leaving 52. Then 13 groups of 4 remove the rest. The partial quotients 200 + 13 make the quotient 213.

predict.prompt: Taking 200 fours out of 852 first, is that legal?

cml.actionGoal: Remove convenient multiples of the divisor, record their group counts as partial quotients, and add those partial quotients to find the total quotient.
invariants: Each removed chunk equals divisor × its partial quotient; all removed chunks plus the remainder equal the dividend, and the partial quotients add to the total quotient.
misconceptions: Recording a removed amount as the partial quotient, choosing a chunk that exceeds what remains, or failing to add every partial quotient breaks the division relationship.

widget.prompt: In 852 ÷ 4, shade a chunk worth 200 groups of 4. Which statement explains why this is a valid first chunk?

options.label: Because any number of groups can be removed at once, in any order
options.feedback: Correct — partial quotients removes convenient chunks and adds them up; the order never changes the total.

options.label: Because 200 is the only correct first chunk
options.feedback: It is convenient, not required — 100 fours twice reaches the same place, just more slowly.

options.label: Because 4 × 200 is bigger than 852
options.feedback: 4 × 200 is 800, which fits inside 852 — that is exactly why the chunk is legal.

options.label: It is not allowed — you must take one group at a time
options.feedback: Taking one at a time works but is enormously slow; chunking is the whole point of the method.
